drills.title: Structured And-proof with case tags
hints: Theorem `test`: for propositions p, q, from hypotheses hp : p and hq : q prove p ∧ (q ∧ p), in tactic mode.
Split the outer conjunction by applying And.intro.
Address the left subgoal by its tag and close it exactly with hp.
Address the right subgoal by its tag: split it again with And.intro, then close its left and right subgoals, each addressed by tag, exactly with hq and hp.

drills.title: Structured And-proof with bullets
hints: Theorem `test`: for propositions p, q, from hp : p and hq : q prove p ∧ (q ∧ p), in tactic mode.
Split the outer conjunction by applying And.intro.
Focus the first subgoal with a bullet and close it exactly with hp.
Focus the second subgoal with a bullet: apply And.intro again, then close its two subgoals with nested bullets, exactly with hq and hp.

drills.title: Reverting and reintroducing a variable
hints: Anonymous example: for x : Nat, prove x = x, in tactic mode.
Revert x, moving it back into the goal.
Introduce it again under the new name y.
Close the goal by reflexivity.

drills.title: Generalizing a constant and restoring it
hints: Anonymous example: prove 2 + 3 = 5, in tactic mode.
Generalize 3 to a fresh variable x, recording the equation 3 = x in a hypothesis named h.
Rewrite with h right to left, which puts 3 back and closes the goal.

drills.title: Closing both disjunction cases at once
hints: Anonymous example: for a proposition p, prove p ∨ p → p, in tactic mode.
Introduce the hypothesis as h.
Do an unstructured case split on h.
Close all resulting goals by repeating assumption.

drills.title: Supplying an explicit existential witness
hints: Anonymous example: for predicates p, q on Nat, prove (∃ x, p x) → ∃ x, p x ∨ q x, in tactic mode.
Introduce the hypothesis as h.
Case on h with a named alternative for its constructor intro, binding x and px.
In that alternative, all on one line: give x as the witness using the exists tactic, apply Or.inl, then close exactly with px.

drills.title: Destructuring nested existential and conjunction
hints: Anonymous example: for predicates p, q on Nat, prove (∃ x, p x ∧ q x) → ∃ x, q x ∧ p x, in tactic mode.
Introduce the hypothesis as h.
Case on h with the named alternative for constructor intro, binding x and hpq.
Inside it, case on hpq with the named alternative for constructor intro, binding hp and hq.
Inside that, finish with the exists tactic giving witness x; it discharges the remaining conjunction by itself.

drills.title: Distributing and over or, brace-structured
hints: Anonymous example: for propositions p, q, r, prove p ∧ (q ∨ r) ↔ (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r), in tactic mode, structuring every subproof with curly-brace blocks and separating tactics with semicolons.
Apply Iff.intro.
Forward block: introduce h, then do an unstructured case split on the right component of h.

Forward, each of the two sub-blocks: state the goal (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r) with show, then close exactly with the left (resp. right) injection of the pair made of h's left component and the anonymous hypothesis q (resp. r), referred to by its type.
Backward block: introduce h, then do an unstructured case split on h.

Backward, each of the two sub-blocks: state the goal p ∧ (q ∨ r) with show, name the inaccessible hypothesis hpq (resp. hpr) using rename_i, then close exactly with the pair of its left component and Or.inl (resp. Or.inr) of its right component.

drills.title: One-line conjunction proof with try
hints: Anonymous example: for propositions p, q, r with hp : p, hq : q, hr : r, prove p ∧ q ∧ r, in tactic mode, in one line.

Apply constructor; then, on every goal it produces, try constructor (parenthesised); then, on every goal that produces, use assumption. Chain these with the combinator that runs the next tactic on all goals produced by the previous one.

drills.title: Applying tactics to all goals
hints: Anonymous example: for propositions p, q, r with hp : p, hq : q, hr : r, prove p ∧ q ∧ r, in tactic mode.
Apply constructor.
On all open goals, try constructor (parenthesised).
On all open goals, use assumption.

drills.title: Proving a nested conjunction in one line
hints: Anonymous example: for propositions p, q, r with hp : p, hq : q, hr : r, prove p ∧ ((p ∧ q) ∧ r) ∧ (q ∧ r ∧ p), in tactic mode.
In a single line: repeatedly, on any goals, try first constructor and, if that fails, assumption (parenthesise each layer).

drills.title: Rewriting the type of a hypothesis
hints: Define Tuple, taking α : Type and n : Nat, as the subtype of lists as : List α whose length equals n.
Anonymous example: for n : Nat, h : n = 0 and t : Tuple α n (leave α auto-bound), produce a Tuple α 0, in tactic mode.
Rewrite with h in the hypothesis t.
Close exactly with t.

drills.title: Simplifying hypotheses and goal together
hints: Locally add Nat.mul_comm, Nat.mul_assoc and Nat.mul_left_comm to the simp set.
In a second line, likewise locally add Nat.add_assoc, Nat.add_comm and Nat.add_left_comm.
Anonymous example: for w x y z : Nat, a predicate p on Nat, and h : p (x * y + z * w * x), prove p (x * w * z + y * x), in tactic mode.
On one line: simplify at every hypothesis and the goal, then finish with assumption.
Anonymous example: for x y z : Nat, a predicate p on Nat, h₁ : p (1 * x + y) and h₂ : p (x * z * 1), prove p (y + 0 + x) ∧ p (z * x), in tactic mode.
On one line: simplify everywhere, then constructor on every resulting goal, then assumption on every resulting goal.

drills.title: Splitting a match and discharging cases
hints: Anonymous example: for x y z : Nat (leave w auto-bound), prove x ≠ 5 → y ≠ 5 → z ≠ 5 → z = w → f x y w = 1, in tactic mode, all on one line.
Introduce all the hypotheses with intros, leaving them unnamed.
Simplify, unfolding f.
Split on the match; on each resulting goal, try contradiction first and rfl if that fails.

drills.title: Registering a lemma for simp
hints: Theorem `reverse_mk_symm`, marked as a simplification rule where it is declared: for xs : List α, the reverse of mk_symm xs (taken with dot notation) equals mk_symm xs.
Prove it in tactic mode with simp, giving it mk_symm to unfold.
Anonymous example: for xs ys : List Nat, the reverse of xs ++ mk_symm ys equals mk_symm ys ++ the reverse of xs (both reverses by dot notation). Prove it with plain simp.
Anonymous example: for xs ys : List Nat, a predicate p : List Nat → Prop and h : p applied to the reverse of xs ++ mk_symm ys, prove p (mk_symm ys ++ the reverse of xs).
In tactic mode, on one line: simplify the hypothesis h, then close the goal with assumption.
